pactus1.definition: pactus adj. P. of paciscor, agreed, settled, determined, covenanted, stipulated : pro capite pretium: pacta et constituta cum Manlio dies: merces, H.: coniunx, betrothed , V.

palam1.definition: palam adj., openly, publicly, undisguisedly, plainly: nihil ausurus, S.: ad se adire, Cs.: quae in foro palam gesta sunt: agere: non per praestigias, sed palam: palam et aperte dicere: Luce palam, V.: palam duobus exe…

palam2.definition: palam praep., with abl. 1 palam, before, in the presence of : te palam, H.: Marte palam, O.: rem creditori palam populo solvit, L.

percussus2.definition: percussus ūs, m percutio, a beating, striking : Percussu crebro saxa cavantur, O.

permissus1.definition: permissus P. of permitto.—As subst n., a permission: utor permisso, H.

permissus2.definition: (permissus, ūs) m per+MIT-, leave, permission ; only abl: permissu legis: Lentuli, L.

pessime1.definition: pessimē see malus, badly, wrongly, ill, wretchedly : homines male vestiti: animo malest? are you vexed? T.: hoc male habet virum, vexes , T.: L. Antonio male sit, ill betide : audire, be ill-spoken of.— Badly, wickedl…

pessime2.definition: pessimē pessimus, sup. of male, malus.

pinna1.definition: pinna ae, f SPI-, a feather, plume (upon a bird; see also penna): (aves) pullos pinnis fovent.— A wing (only plur.): O Fides alma apta pinnis: pinnis coruscant (apes), V.: non pinnis sublime elatos Alpīs transgressos,…

plausus2.definition: plausus ūs, m plaudo, a clapping, flapping, noise from striking : plausu premunt alas (of cocks), Enn. ap. C.: ingens (of doves), V.— A clapping of hands in approval, applause : plausū s cupiditas: a plebe plausu maxi…

plus1.definition: plūs plūris (plur. plūres, plūra, gen. plūrium), adj. PLE-. I. Sing. n as subst, more : ne quid faciam plus, too much , T.: tantum et plus etiam ipse mihi deberet: vos et decem numero, et, quod plus est, Romani estis,…

plus2.definition: plūs adv. sing n. of 1 plus, more (used as comp. of multum, with sup. plurimum): apud me argumenta plus quam testes valent: plus quam semel, more often : nulla (navis) plus quam triginta remis agatur, L.: Plus miliens…

pone1.definition: pōne adv. POS-, after, behind, back : adprendit pallio, T.: et ante et pone (moveri): sequens, V.

pone2.definition: pōne praep. with acc. 1 pone, behind : pone quos aut ante labantur: pone castra, L.

porrectus2.definition: porrēctus adj. with comp. P. of 1 porrigo, stretched out, extended, long : loca, Cs.: locus, H.: mora, protracted , O.: porrectior acies, Ta.: senex, i. e. dead , Ct.—Fig., wide-spread, extended : fama ad ortum Solis, H.

positus1.definition: positus adj. P. of pono, placed, situated, set, planted, standing, lying : Roma in montibus: tumulus opportune ad id, L.: somno positus (i. e. sopitus), V.

positus2.definition: positus (ūs), m pono, a position, situation, disposition, order, arrangement : siderum, Ta.: positu variare comas, O.: terra a positu nomen adepta loci, O.: tot positū s conprendere, ways of dressing the hair , O.

praegressus2.definition: praegressus ūs praegredior, an advance : rerum praegressū s, i. e. steps in development .

praepositus1.definition: praepositus adj. P. of praepono, preferable, preferred .—As subst n., that which is desirable (opp. both to the absolete good, and to evil).

praepositus2.definition: praepositus ī, m P. of praepono, a prefect, president, chief : legatorum tuorum.

praetextus1.definition: praetextus adj. P. of praetexo, bordered, edged : toga, bordered with purple (worn by the higher magistrates; also by free-born children less than seventeen years of age): aedilicia: togae praetextae habendae ius, L.:…

praetextus2.definition: (praetextus, ūs) m TEC-, a show, display, pretence, pretext (only abl sing .): sub leni praetextu verborum, L.: praetextu senatūs, Ta.

pressus1.definition: pressus adj. with comp. P. of premo, closed, close, shut tight : presso obmutuit ore, V.: oscula iungere pressa, i. e. ardent , O.: presso gutture, i. e. hoarsely , V.— Repressed, suppressed, kept down, slow : pede pr…

pressus2.definition: pressus ūs, m PREM-, a pressing, pressure : ponderum: palmarum, C. poët.—Fig.: ipso oris pressu et sono, i. e. expression .

pro2.definition: prō praep. with abl. PRO-.—Of place, before, in front of, in face of : sedens pro aede Castoris: pro castris dimicare, Cs.: castra pro moenibus locata, L.: pro castris suas copias produxit, before the camp , Cs.: pro …

pro3.definition: prō (not prōh), interj., of wonder or lamentation, O! Ah! Alas!: pro, quanta potentia regni Est tui! O.: tantum, pro! degeneramus a patribus, L.: pro di inmortales: Pro curia inversique mores! H.: pro divom fidem! T.:…

prod-.definition: prōd- old form of pro, in prod-eo, prod-est.

provisus2.definition: (prōvīsus ūs), m pro+VID-.—Only abl. sing., a looking forward, distant view : ne oculi provisu iuvabant, Ta.— A foreseeing : periculi, Ta. — A caring for beforehand , Ta.
